clue.text: Thank you, and goodbye!

definitions.meaning: a casual British word of gratitude, like ta
also said in Britain as an informal farewell, like cheerio

explanation.definitionFit: The same informal British word serves both as thanks and as a parting farewell.

clue.text: House-warming arranged for Alice

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, as with these letters

explanation.surface: A party to warm a new house is organised for a woman named Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House-warming' looks like a party; read literally, it is something that heats a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A grate burning lumps of carbon fuel literally warms a house.

clue.text: He used tax form that's expired

indicators.note: form here is a verb, to shape these letters into something new, though it poses as a tax form

explanation.surface: A tax return he filed has passed its deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something used up or worn out to the end has run out, like an expired supply.

clue.text: Grass blown in the wind

definitions.meaning: a tall grass growing by water
the wind section of an orchestra, where the vibrating strip in a clarinet or oboe is blown

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a waterside grass and the vibrating strip in woodwind instruments.

clue.text: Deportment of unusual air and grace

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of the following words are set out in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Someone's bearing is praised for an uncommon airy gracefulness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe the way a person holds and moves their body, their posture.

clue.text: Refuse to vote, putting Jack on the spot

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
a spot is a mark or stain

explanation.surface: A man named Jack is put on the spot when asked to vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to decline deliberately to cast a ballot either for or against a motion.

clue.text: Puzzle that has many twists and turns before being solved

definitions.text: Puzzle that has many twists and turns before being solved

parts.words: Puzzle that has many twists and turns before being solved
parts.note: a coloured cube whose faces are physically twisted until each side is one colour

explanation.walkthrough: 'twists and turns' suggests a convoluted plot; here they are literal rotations of the toy's layers.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Hungarian puzzle toy is solved by rotating its layers many times.

clue.text: It might be proof of convenient absence

definitions.text: It might be proof of convenient absence

parts.words: It might be proof of convenient absence
parts.note: evidence of being elsewhere when a crime was committed

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for elsewhere names the defence that one was absent from the crime scene.

clue.text: They keep a sharp eye on German and US arms

definitions.meaning: birds of prey famous for keen eyesight
arms in the heraldic sense: both national coats of arms show this bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons; it means coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Large keen-sighted raptors appear on the national emblems of both Germany and the United States.

clue.text: They may be spun to make briefs

definitions.text: They may be spun to make briefs

indicators.note: spun means twisted round, so the letters of the last word are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: Threads are spun before being woven into underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and 'may be spun' also rearranges the letters of briefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Threads are spun to make yarn, which is woven into fabric for underwear.

clue.text: His cattle wandered on the track, perhaps

indicators.note: cattle that wandered strayed about, so these letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A farmer's herd has strayed onto a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The track looks like a railway or a farm path; here it is the running track, standing for the sport as a whole, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Track events are one part of the sport of running, jumping and throwing, so the track is an example of it.

clue.text: Conduct British band

parts.note: a ring is a circular band, as on a finger

explanation.surface: An instruction to lead a group of British musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to conduct someone somewhere is to escort or take them along.

clue.text: Outlet for dispersing fuel

indicators.note: dispersing scatters things, so the letters of the next word are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A vent or chimney through which burnt fuel escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct is the outlet that carries smoke and gases away from a fire.

clue.text: A beef drink prepared and used in the kitchen

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been made ready, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A beefy drink such as a broth is made up and served in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated slicing implement for loaves is a utensil found in the kitchen.

clue.text: Cook sizing a cod or fishes, for example

indicators.note: to cook figures or food is to work them over, so these letters are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe tells the cook to cut a cod or other fish to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishes' looks like more food for the cook; it is Pisces, the sign of the two fishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces, depicted as two fishes, is one of the twelve astrological star signs.

clue.text: Fare allowances

definitions.meaning: fare means food provided, as in plain fare
fixed allowances or shares, as of food in wartime

explanation.definitionFit: Fixed food portions are both the fare eaten and an allowance doled out to each person.

clue.text: One stealing a pound?

definitions.meaning: to nick is British slang for to steal, so one who nicks is a thief
British slang for one pound sterling

explanation.definitionFit: British slang gives the same word for a petty thief and for a pound note or coin.

clue.text: Come in, it is not an infectious disease

explanation.surface: A doctor welcomes a patient, reassuring them the illness is not contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is simply 'Come in' plus 'it is'; the definition is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the small intestine, often from irritants or diet rather than any contagion.

clue.text: Nuts and biscuits

definitions.meaning: thin dry savoury biscuits, often eaten with cheese

explanation.definitionFit: The same word is British slang for mad and the name for dry savoury biscuits.

clue.text: Unrehearsed parts of the actor's speech

definitions.text: Unrehearsed parts of the actor's speech

parts.words: Unrehearsed parts of the actor's speech
parts.note: lines an actor improvises on stage rather than learning from the script

explanation.definitionFit: Improvised remarks an actor makes up on the spot are by nature not rehearsed.

clue.text: Bob, of English origin

indicators.note: origin marks the word as the source from which these letters are made, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Bob is said to come from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A short tapered hairstyle of the 1920s is closely related to the bob cut.

clue.text: One arguing re a debt unsettled

indicators.note: a debt left unsettled is unresolved, and the letters are likewise disturbed into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: A person who argues a case in a formal discussion is a debater.

clue.text: Died in a city in Natal

annotationWithheld.why: Died in a city in Natal (6): D + URBAN (in a city) needs 'city' again for the definition 'city in Natal', so 'city' does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Died in a city in Natal

clue.text: Like a neighbour being present

definitions.meaning: a neighbour is close by, nearby

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both near by in place, as a neighbour is, and present or available now.

clue.text: Old-fashioned news broadcasters

parts.note: officials who once walked the streets calling out public announcements

explanation.definitionFit: Before newspapers and radio, town officials rang a bell and shouted proclamations to spread news.

clue.text: Winds blow in the west and south

indicators.note: in means the blow is placed inside the two compass points

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
a rap is a sharp blow or knock

explanation.surface: Gusts blow through western and southern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' reads as gales; it is the verb, as when one winds a bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to wind cloth around something is to wrap it.

clue.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

definitions.text: If there's a man around, he's from the US

parts.words: If there's a man around, he's from the US
parts.note: put the letters of 'a man' either side of this name, AM before and AN after, and the result is a word for a US citizen

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a man around' literally: wrap A-M ... A-N about the man's name and you get a word meaning someone from the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A common boy's name, which sits inside the word for a native of the United States.

clue.text: Punishment for a murderer, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the answer sounds like a word, not spelt like it

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A suitable penalty for a killer is proposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating with a stick was a traditional school punishment.

clue.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

definitions.text: On which adders slide to and fro?

parts.words: On which adders slide to and fro?
parts.note: adders here are people doing sums, sliding beads back and forth on counting frames

explanation.walkthrough: 'adders' suggests snakes; read it as people who add up figures on counting frames.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting frames with beads on wires, the plural of the Latin-derived word, are used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Undertake to back mount and argue wildly about it

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the reversed mountain
wildly signals the letters of argue are thrown into a disordered arrangement
back means the mountain's name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Etna is the volcano on Sicily

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to support a climb, then argues fiercely over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the reversed mountain, ANTE, which the anagram GUARE wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a formal promise that something will happen is to undertake it.

clue.text: Give someone a lift from the cemetery

definitions.text: Give someone a lift from the cemetery

parts.words: Give someone a lift from the cemetery
parts.note: a lift here is raising a body out of its grave, not a ride in a car

explanation.walkthrough: 'Give someone a lift' suggests a car ride home; it means digging a buried body up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up a buried corpse, literally lifting it out of the ground.

clue.text: It comes between opposing sides

parts.note: the word printed between two teams' names on a fixture list, like 'v'

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for against stands between the names of rival teams or legal parties.
